what_it_does: Datalog is a logic-programming language used in program analysis, security auditing, and database query processing; it works by repeatedly applying rules to a set of known facts until no new facts can be derived. GPUs (graphics processors) are extremely good at doing many operations in parallel on dense, regular data, but Datalog's fact sets are sparse (most possible combinations are absent) and grow irregularly as rules fire, making them poorly suited to the regular data structures GPUs prefer. GPUlog addresses this by introducing a new data structure called a Hash-Indexed Sorted Array (HISA) that indexes a sorted list of facts with a hash table, letting the GPU efficiently find relevant entries and incrementally add new ones during each round of rule application. All the core relational operations — joining two fact sets, combining them, subtracting facts already known — are implemented over this structure in ways that exploit GPU parallelism, enabling the engine to run the standard semi-naive Datalog evaluation algorithm (which only processes newly derived facts each round rather than reprocessing everything) entirely on the GPU with a much smaller memory footprint than prior GPU hash-join approaches.
